fatal_errors: The proposed bulk, as-cast experimental alloy does not reconstruct the single-crystal FCC molecular-dynamics model.
It omits the crystallographic-orientation, temperature, and high-strain-rate parameter sweeps central to the target method.
It does not test the target mechanisms involving vacancy-associated nucleation, Shockley partials, stacking faults, or exclusion of BCC transformation and twinning.
The sole cited evidence concerns a chemically and structurally different refractory HEA and cannot substantiate mechanical predictions for FeNiCrMn.
The falsification criterion relies on an undefined expected range from analogous alloys and therefore is weakly discriminating.
explanation: Standard tensile testing is a reasonable alternative for obtaining macroscopic mechanical properties, so the response broadly addresses the knowledge gap. However, it does not reconstruct the target molecular-dynamics study of an equiatomic FCC FeNiCrMn single crystal loaded along <110>, <1-12>, and <-111> over 10–600 K and 10^8–10^10 s^-1. Consequently, it misses the predicted anisotropy, thermal softening, strain-rate-insensitive yield strength, rate-dependent dislocation density, and Shockley-partial/stacking-fault mechanism. Its evidence supports only the generic feasibility of tensile testing in another HEA system, not the claimed behavior of FeNiCrMn.
